newsitem.title: USA: Caliber System says to sell part of Viking.
newsitem.headline: Caliber System says to sell part of Viking.

text.p: Caliber System Inc said on Wednesday that it had reached an agreement in principal to sell Viking Freight's southwestern division to a group consisting of outside investors and senior management from the division's former carrier, Central Freight Lines.
Central Freight Lines was consolidated into Viking Freight in 1996, the company said. Viking Freight, in turn, is an operating company of Caliber.
On March 27, Caliber announced the major restructuring of Viking Freight and in its first quarter earnings results it reported a $85 million charge related to the restructuring.
The Central group is led by Joe Hall, who is the division's current vice president of operations and will become the company's president, Caliber said in a statement.
Under the terms of the agreement, the investor group will operate 57 terminals and other related assets, including rolling stock, the company said.
The transaction, which has been approved by Caliber's board of directors, is subject to the signing of a definitive agreement and normal regulatory approval, it added.

"With the sale of the former Central, the restructuring of Viking is now complete," said Caliber president and chief executive Daniel Sullivan. "We expect the unit as it is now configured to earn an operating profit in the fourth quarter of this year."
Caliber System provides transportation, logistics and related information services.
Viking Freight, based in California, provides next- and second-day less-than-truckload service.
